title: Nuevo Laredo Launches Voluntary Gun Buyback: Cash for Firearms, No Questions Asked
excerpt: Mexico's Defense Ministry and the Nuevo Laredo municipal government launched a voluntary firearms exchange on Tuesday, offering cash for guns turned in for destruction, with no questions asked and no investigation, through Nov. 24 at the Esteban Baca Calderón plaza, according to Sin Censura.
content:
Mexico's Defense Ministry and the Nuevo Laredo municipal government launched a voluntary firearms exchange on Tuesday, Nov. 17, offering cash for guns turned in for destruction, with no questions asked and no investigation, according to Sin Censura.

The campaign, under the slogan “Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz” (Yes to Disarmament, Yes to Peace), runs Nov. 17 through Nov. 24 at the Esteban Baca Calderón plaza, where a collection module has been installed, according to the report.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas and Gen. Humberto Ortega Ramírez, commander of the military garrison, opened the campaign at a ceremony at the plaza, according to the report. Gen. Ortega said the campaign is an opportunity to strengthen a culture of prevention, encourage citizen participation and help build a safer, more peaceful environment for Nuevo Laredo families.

Residents are invited to turn in firearms, cartridges and other weapons kept at home, anonymously and safely, with no legal consequences, in order to prevent accidents and acts of violence, according to the report.

The first weapon turned in was destroyed in full before members of the media: a 7.62 rifle, described as neglected but still serviceable, for which the person who turned it in received a little more than 13,000 pesos, according to the report. Those who turn in a weapon also receive a certificate of total destruction.

Sources: Sin Censura, Nov. 17, 2026.
